title: Read-only share links for project boards
brief: Board owners can now create share links, which let anyone view a board without signing in. Owners choose when each link expires, and they can turn it off at any time.
background: Teamboard is a small app for project boards. Until now every board was private: only members of a project could see it. A member's role (owner, editor, or viewer) decides what they may do. Each route looks up that role with `roleFor` in `permissions.ts` and refuses the request if the role doesn't allow it.

terms.means: A URL that lets anyone open one board, read-only, without signing in.
The random secret at the end of a share link (`/s/<token>`). Whoever has it can view the board.
Turn a link off. The row stays in `share_links` with a `revoked_at` time; it isn't deleted.
A link that hasn't been revoked and hasn't passed its expiry date.
The new permission check for creating and revoking links. Only owners pass it.

risk.why: Adds the first route that works without signing in (`GET /s/:token`). It also has two bugs: choosing *Never* still creates a 7-day link, and a board whose links have all expired still shows as shared.

ask: Look closely at `GET /s/:token`. It is the first route that doesn't require signing in.
A skim is enough for the popover and the header. They display data and pass the owner's choices up to their parent.
summary: A new `share_links` table holds one row per link: a hash of its token, its expiry date, and when it was revoked.
Projects get a `visibility` column. It is `private`, or `link` while the board has a live link.
Three new routes. Owners can create and revoke links, and anyone with a link can view the board at `GET /s/:token`.
A new `canShare` permission lets owners share. Editors can still rename a board but can't share it.
The project header gets a **Share** button for owners and a *Shared by link* badge. The button opens a popover for managing links.

entities.name: share_links
entities.note: One row per link. The raw token is never stored.

fields.name: project_id
fields.note: Deleted with its project (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). Indexed.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.note: Empty means the link never expires

fields.note: Set when the link is revoked. The row is kept.

fields.note: Defaults to `private`, so existing rows need no update

blocks.title: The migration only adds
blocks.md: `002_share_links.sql` creates a table and adds a column with a default. Nothing is dropped or rewritten, and there is no down migration.

blocks.summary: Unchanged, but deleting a project's links depends on it.

annotations.text: SQLite ignores foreign keys unless this setting is on. Without it, deleting a project would leave its links behind.

endpoints.summary: Create a link. The response holds the raw token inside `url`, and this is the only time the server sends it.

params.name: ttlDays
params.note: How many days the link lasts. Defaults to 7. The popover sends `null` for *Never*.

endpoints.summary: Revoke a link. The row is kept and marked revoked. If no live links remain, the project goes back to `private`.
Look up a token and return the board, read-only. Unknown, expired, and revoked tokens all get the same 404.

blocks.caption: How a visitor's request is handled. The token is hashed before the lookup, so the raw token never reaches the database.
blocks.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant V as Link visitor
  participant R as GET /s/:token
  participant S as resolveShareLink
  participant DB as share_links
  V->>R: /s/k3J9…x2Qa
  R->>S: token
  S->>S: sha256(token)
  S->>DB: WHERE token_hash = ?
  DB-->>S: row or nothing
  alt revoked, expired, or missing
    S-->>R: null
    R-->>V: 404 link_not_found
  else live
    S-->>R: { projectId }
    R-->>V: 200 { id, name } read-only
  end

keyChanges.summary: Adds three routes: create a link, revoke a link, and the public page for a link. Create and revoke require `canShare`; the public route needs no sign-in.

annotations.text: This checks `canShare`, not `canEdit`, so editors get a 403 here.
`req.body.ttlDays ?? 7` replaces `null` with 7, and `null` is what the popover sends for *Never*. Use `'ttlDays' in req.body ? req.body.ttlDays : 7` to keep an explicit `null`.
annotations.title: *Never* becomes 7 days

annotations.text: This response is the only place the raw token leaves the server.
The public route. It selects only `id` and `name`, so it can't expose what's on the board. Unknown, expired, and revoked tokens all get the same 404, so a visitor can't tell which case they hit.

keyChanges.summary: A new module for the whole life of a link: create it, check it on each visit, and revoke it. It also keeps `projects.visibility` up to date.

annotations.text: Tokens are hashed before they are stored, so a leaked database doesn't give anyone working links.
24 random bytes, written as 32 URL-safe characters. That is 192 bits, far too many to guess.
The insert and the visibility update don't run in one transaction. That's fine on SQLite in practice. If this moves to Postgres, wrap them in `db.transaction`.
Expiry is checked when a link is used. Nothing deletes old rows.
This counts links that aren't revoked, but it ignores `expires_at`. When every link has simply expired, the project stays `link` and keeps showing *Shared by link*.
annotations.title: Expired links keep a board shared

keyChanges.summary: The header shows the *Shared by link* badge, and a **Share** button for owners that opens the popover.

annotations.text: The component repeats the `canShare` rule instead of importing it. The server still enforces the real check.
The badge follows `project.visibility`, which `shareLinks.ts` keeps up to date.

keyChanges.summary: One new permission, for owners only.

annotations.text: Deliberately stricter than `canEdit`: editors can't share.

keyChanges.summary: Creates `share_links` and adds `projects.visibility` with a default, so existing rows need no update.

annotations.text: A project's links are deleted along with it.
SQLite allows adding a column with a `CHECK` here because the default value passes the check.
